method: Rare-Regime Agent + dynamic Tail allocation diagnostic v1
note: No draw 2146 result used. Candidate-space evaluation uses a fixed deterministic 11,998-combination sample, so results are comparative diagnostics, not exact full-space performance.

dynamic_allocation_test_1.symmetric_dynamic: Low: 8 Main+1 BandTail+1 FlowTail; Mid: fixed; High: 4 Main+2 BandTail+2 FlowTail+1 GapTail+1 DeepTail
dynamic_allocation_test_1.conclusion: Rejected. Reducing Tail coverage in low-risk draws hurt more than high-risk expansion helped.

dynamic_allocation_test_2.high_risk_threshold: top quartile of train Rare Risk, cutoff=1.363
dynamic_allocation_test_2.principle: One-sided intervention only; low/mid retain the fixed portfolio.
dynamic_allocation_test_2.dev_selected: H3 = on high-risk draws, 5 Main + 1 BandTail + 1 FlowTail + 1 GapTail + 2 DeepTail
dynamic_allocation_test_2.exploratory_best_on_test_not_selected: H4 = 4 Main + 2 BandTail + 2 FlowTail + 1 GapTail + 1 DeepTail gave d3plus 111 and recall6 39, but lost one d4 and was not selected on dev, so it is not adopted.
dynamic_allocation_test_2.conclusion: One-sided DeepTail boost is mildly promising but not robust enough to replace the fixed portfolio. Keep as research branch / forward test.

next_steps: Do not reduce Tail lanes just because Rare Risk is low.
Use Rare-Regime only as a one-sided boost when confidence is high.
Predict coarse anomaly types (Band concentration, F1+F2 depletion/F5-heavy Flow, bimodal Gap) rather than exact rare states.
Optimize for preserving d4+ while improving d3+ and Winner Number Recall; avoid a Tail boost that trades away d4.
Forward-test the dev-selected H3 rule before adopting it.
